title: Base Digit Validator
statement:
Decide whether a piece of text is a valid unsigned whole number in a chosen base.

Contract
- `digits` may be any `String`; `base` must be between 2 and 36 inclusive.
- Digits `0` through `9` have values 0 through 9, and letters `A` through `Z` or `a` through `z` have values 10 through 35.
- A leading `0x` or `0X` is allowed only when `base == 16`, and at least one digit must remain after the prefix.
- Return `true` only when every remaining character is a digit whose value is strictly less than `base`. Null, empty text, signs, spaces, underscores, and invalid bases return `false`.

Examples
- `isValidForBase("10110", 2)` returns `true`.
- `isValidForBase("0Xff", 16)` returns `true`.
- `isValidForBase("128", 8)` returns `false`.
hints: Convert each character to its numeric value instead of building a list of all valid characters.
Handle the optional hexadecimal prefix before checking the remaining digits.
Reject invalid bases and use `Character.digit(ch, base)` or equivalent logic. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
inputSyntax: Input: digits followed by base, for example: 0xFF 16
